lines: “《修仙OL》——一款百分百真实的虚拟现实开放世界修仙游戏。”
“现游戏正在招募内测玩家，带你亲身领略仙侠世界的极致魅力。”
一则这样的广告突然出现在地球网络上。
词儿挺短，但吹嘘的力度却大到没边。
百分百真实？
虚拟现实游戏？
眼下就连最基础的VR技术都还不成熟呢。
这广告口气大得仿佛直接从科幻片场穿越来的。
但偏偏在各大论坛、社交平台、甚至一些正经的技术社区角落，都能看到它的身影
删不完，禁不绝。
好奇的人顺着广告摸了过去，却只有一个十分干净的所谓“官方网站”
界面简陋得感人。
除了那几句牛逼哄哄的宣传语和一个孤零零的报名入口，连张像样的原画，一段哪怕是CG冒充的演示视频都没有。
域名也古怪，一串毫无规律的字符，像是随手乱打的。
“好家伙，这网页是用脚做的吗？成本不超过十块钱吧？”
“笑死，现在的骗局都这么不走心了吗？连个充值入口都懒得做，差评！”
“查不到备案，IP跳来跳去，服务器估计在太平洋某小岛的黑网吧里吧。”
“散了散了，估计是骗个人信息的，谁报名谁傻叉。”
“现在连脑机接口都没影呢，还百分百虚拟现实，你怎么不直接说能带我原地飞升呢？”
网友们一边倒地嘲讽，乐子人们则是截图调侃。
确实。
这玩意儿从里到外都透着一股强烈的不靠谱气息。
像极了那种骗到邮箱就给你狂发垃圾广告的拙劣陷阱。
但世界大了，总有那么些不信邪，或者单纯无聊到想看看骗子到底想干嘛的人。
大学宿舍里，刚肝完论文的李铭揉着酸涩的眼睛，鼠标在那简陋的报名页面上晃了半天。
最终嗤笑一声。
还是顺手填了个自己的邮箱和游戏名“剑斩红尘”
，点了提交。
“呵，我倒要看看你能玩出什么花来?”
写字楼隔间里，摸鱼的白领赵莎被KPI压得喘不过气，鬼使神差地对着那报名表发了几秒呆。
敲下了“琉璃仙梦”
这个高中中二时期用过的ID。
content_en:
""Cultivation of Immortality OL" - a 100% real virtual reality open world cultivation game."
"Now the game is recruiting closed beta players to take you to experience the ultimate charm of the Xianxia world."
An advertisement like this suddenly appeared on the Earth Network.
The words are quite short, but the bragging power is endless.
One hundred percent true?
Virtual reality game?
Even the most basic VR technology is not mature yet.
The tone of this advertisement is as loud as if it came directly from a science fiction set.
But it can be seen in major forums, social platforms, and even in some serious technical communities.
It can’t be deleted completely, and it can’t be banned forever.
Curious people followed the advertisement, but there was only a very clean so-called "official website"
The interface is touchingly crude.
Apart from a few cool slogans and a lonely registration entrance, there is not even a decent original painting or even a demonstration video of CG impersonation.
The domain name is also weird, a string of irregular characters, as if it was typed randomly.
"Good guy, is this webpage made of feet? It costs no more than ten yuan, right?"
"It's so funny, are all scams nowadays so careless? They don't even bother to make a recharge entrance, bad review!"
"I can't find the registration. The IP bounces around. The server is probably in a dark Internet cafe on a small island in the Pacific."
"It's over, it's over. They probably cheated on their personal information. Whoever signed up will be stupid."
"There's not even a brain-computer interface now, and it's 100% virtual reality. Why don't you just say you can take me up where I am?"
Netizens ridiculed it, while people took screenshots to make fun of it.
really.
This thing exudes a strong aura of unreliability from the inside out.
It’s like the kind of clumsy trap that tricks you into sending spam ads to your email address.
But the world is big, and there are always some people who don’t believe in evil, or who are simply bored and want to see what the scammers want to do.
In the university dormitory, Li Ming, who had just finished his thesis, rubbed his sore eyes and hovered the mouse on the simple registration page for a long time.
Finally scoffed.
I just filled in my email address and game name "Sword Cuts the Red Dust"
, click Submit.
"Heh, I want to see what tricks you can come up with?"
In the cubicle of the office building, Zhao Sha, a white-collar worker who was trying to get things done, was overwhelmed by the KPIs. She accidentally stared at the registration form for a few seconds.
Knocked down the "glazed fairy dream"
This is the ID I used when I was a sophomore in high school.
